digest.component_or_area: source comment quality gate and CI validator
propositions: Source code comments contain unresolvable commit SHAs, run/thread IDs, and dated incident narratives that decay with time and retention windows, creating maintenance debt and obscuring current state.

A detector scanning for rot-prone tokens (hex SHA-like strings ≥7 chars, run/job/thread IDs ≥8 digits, date+incident-verb patterns) identifies ~16-17 violating comment blocks in the tree that require remediation.

The CI guard must reject reintroduced rot-prone references while accepting durable alternatives: ticket/epic/story IDs, behavioral descriptions, and escape-hatch marked external refs; word-triple aliases must not match path/extension contexts.

All detector hits must be remediated into one of three sanctioned forms: cite a resolvable ticket ID, drop the rot-prone token leaving current-state prose, or replace SHA narratives with behavioral descriptions findable via git log.
The detector's own unit-test module is excluded from tree scans, with zero in-tree escape-hatch suppressions enforced as policy.
False-accept bugs in the alias-pattern matching and race conditions with concurrent commits require tightening the acceptor logic and adding gotcha coverage to prevent post-merge rot injection.
